en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Parks, 59.
The Training Rule on Approaching for Advice.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs neither asked about the Uposatha nor requested the exhortation.
The bhikkhus complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs neither ask about the Uposatha nor request the exhortation? ... [as before] ...
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs neither inquire about the Uposatha nor request instruction?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
“How, monks, can it be that the bhikkhunīs neither inquire about the Uposatha nor request the exhortation?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And so, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule:”

“Every half-month, two things should be expected from the community of monks by a bhikkhunī: the inquiry regarding the uposatha and the approaching for the exhortation. For one who lets this lapse, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Every half-month” means every uposatha day.
"Uposatha" means two kinds of Uposatha: that on the fourteenth day and that on the fifteenth day.
"Exhortation" (ovāda) means...
The eight *garudhammas*:
“I will not ask about the *uposatha* nor request the exhortation”—at the mere act of relinquishing this burden, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
There is no offense:
If there is an obstacle,
and having sought one, she does not obtain a companion nun,
because she is ill.
In cases of misfortune,
for one who is insane,
and for one who is a first-time offender.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
